result.title: Runtime Control for AI Agents: Closing the Evaluation--Execution Gap in Operational Workflows
result.summary: Language-model agents increasingly participate in operational workflows where approvals, binds, and payments create commitments. An approval valid when issued may no longer authorize execution after relevant facts, evidence, policy, or authority change. We call this the evaluation--execution gap. We specify a state-bound runtime assurance layer that separates probabilistic measurement from deterministic adjudication, binds an execution allowance to the decision-relevant basis of an approval, invalidates that allowance after relevant logged changes, and rechecks admissibility at dispatch. This distinguishes the continued validity of a prior approval from a current-state policy check. We describe eight failure modes, an assurance model, a reference architecture, and prospective interventions with retrospective remediation. In a scripted 42-case replay, the state-bound configuration identifies 15 later-invalidated approvals that a deliberately non-re-evaluating point-in-time comparator does not revisit; it holds 14 affected actions before dispatch and compensates one landed effect. These results illustrate behavior under the stipulated policies and event orders, not superiority over dispatch-time enforcement designs or production effectiveness. Under explicit interception, ingestion, dependency, and serialization assumptions, the model establishes dispatch-time validity within the registered execution surface.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对智能体在运维工作流中「批准时有效、执行时可能失效」的评估—执行差距，提出状态绑定的运行时保障层：将概率性测量与确定性裁决分离，把执行许可绑定到批准所依据的决策相关事实，并在派发前重查可容许性，用 42 例脚本回放演示其行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「测量与裁决分离、执行前依当前状态重查决策依据」的框架，可能为 LVR 中「最终答案是否仍由有效视觉证据支持」以及 STOP/提交门槛的设计提供概念类比，需核查其状态失效判定是否可映射到 latent 证据筛选。
